title: Archive and corpus integrity — depth 1
summary: Recursive target for thread preservation, surviving bundles, manifests, checksums, and cross-copy comparison.

sources.title: Here’s how The Post analyzed Hunter Biden’s laptop

unresolved: No original published checksum manifest was located.
Surviving bundle families have not yet been hashed and clustered.

notes: An absent original checksum is not classified as evidence of fabrication.
Byte-level identity, message authenticity, and claim corroboration remain separate determinations.

data.research_question: Can surviving copies be grouped into byte-identical families and tied to the 2022 archive timeline despite the absence of an original checksum manifest?
objectives: Locate surviving public archive bundles and thread-linked mirrors without redistributing credentials or explicit media.
Compute SHA-256, BLAKE3, byte size, file count, normalized directory-tree hash, and per-file manifests.
Compare Manifest.db rows, attachment hashes, and packaging differences across copies.
Record acquisition URLs, timestamps, transformations, and custody events.
hypotheses: Multiple surviving copies will share a stable core even where packaging and filenames differ.
Per-file and database comparison can recover provenance families without an original root checksum.
excluded_sources: unattributed repackaging with no acquisition record
out_of_scope: asserting package identity without hash comparison

workflow.next_action: Create a capture manifest for each surviving lawful archive copy and cluster copies by normalized file-tree hash.
